requirements.title: Major grade and GPA policy
requirements.summary: Every major specialization course requires C-minus or better, and the major specialization GPA must be at least 2.5. Courses may satisfy only one major/minor specialization or cognate.

requirements.title: Writing, mathematics and prerequisite progression
requirements.summary: Writing requirements must be completed before junior classification, and the specified quantitative requirement before the fifth semester. Follow the current course prerequisites. MGT 401 is taken in the final semester. The mathematics/statistics core rows require C-minus where marked.

requirements.title: BUS 300 writing prerequisite
requirements.summary: Before BUS 300, a student below C-minus in WRS 106 or ENG 106 must repeat one with C-minus or better, or earn C-minus or better in WRS 230.

requirements.title: International-focus requirement
requirements.summary: At least one degree course must have an international focus approved by the Associate Dean of Undergraduate Studies.

requirements.title: AI project and topic restrictions
requirements.summary: BTE 497 and BTE 499 must use AI-focused topics; BUS 428 must use an AI-focused project and requires this declared major and junior standing or higher.

requirements.title: Approved career-course alternative
requirements.summary: MGT 199, BUS 211 or another approved Miami Business School career course can fulfill the career-course requirement.

requirements.title: Cognate fulfillment
requirements.summary: A qualifying major or minor may satisfy an Area of Knowledge. The sample-plan note explains that business majors/minors may satisfy STEM and People and Society; Arts and Humanities must be met outside the business school.

requirements.title: Quantitative choice approval and overlap
requirements.summary: The suggested quantitative-choice courses require Associate Dean approval and appropriate prerequisites. BTE 324/BTE 423 cannot also meet the major requirement unless Business Technology is an additional business major.

requirements.title: Transfer eligibility and residency
requirements.summary: At least half of the credits in each major and minor must be completed through Miami; departments may require more. Transfer work must fall within ten years of initial Miami bachelor matriculation, with approved accreditation and faculty-approved equivalence. Only letter-graded work at C or better is eligible; C-minus, pass/fail and satisfactory/unsatisfactory work do not qualify. Upper-division equivalence cannot come from a two-year institution.

requirements.title: Transfer approval and repeat exclusions
requirements.summary: Submit outside coursework through MATES and obtain approval before enrolling. Approved equivalence does not by itself establish applicability to a particular credential. Continuing students must send an official transcript by the end of the following semester; incoming students by the end of their first semester. Transfer grades are not in the regular UM GPA. Accepted transfer or examination credit cannot ordinarily be repeated for Miami credit; the source permits a specific program exception that removes examination credit before repeating.

requirements.title: Unresolved summer concurrent-enrollment rule
requirements.summary: The transfer eligibility section excludes summer from its concurrent-enrollment prohibition, while Courses Not Accepted prohibits concurrent outside enrollment and explicitly bars taking a Miami summer Session A course and an outside Session B course. These statements are inconsistent. No summer-transfer permission is inferred; university clarification is required. Business coursework also remains subject to the stricter business residency rule.

requirements.title: Credit-only grading and later major changes
requirements.summary: CR/NC is restricted to free electives rather than major, minor, general education or their prerequisite work. Eligible students must be sophomores or above, have a 3.00 cumulative GPA, and transfer students must first complete a Miami semester; at most one course per semester and nine credits total. A later major change can permit earlier credit-only electives by department-chair and dean discretion. This is not automatic permission for current required coursework.

requirements.title: Approved test credit and GPA treatment
requirements.summary: Accepted AP, IB, GCE, Cambridge Pre-U, CAPE Unit and CLEP equivalents may satisfy requirements with CR despite the ordinary credit-only restriction. CR/NC carries no GPA points. For graduation the university uses the lower of the Miami-only GPA and the combined GPA of Miami and all graded outside work, including work not accepted toward the degree.

requirements.title: General and undergraduate repeat rules
requirements.summary: Ordinarily a course can be repeated once unless the department chair or applicable dean authorizes more; repeatable-for-credit courses are separate. Under the general rule both grades count for D-plus or lower, or C-minus when C is required, and a passing repeat of D/D-plus (or applicable C-minus) increases required graduation hours by the repeated amount. Repeating an already sufficient grade earns no additional credit or GPA points. The undergraduate replacement option covers at most two Miami courses initially graded D/D-plus/F, repeated at Miami as the same course within two enrolled regular semesters; only the second grade counts, even if lower, but the first remains on the transcript. Integrity failures and courses already repeated more than once are excluded. Business-specific restrictions also apply to business coursework.

requirements.title: University graduation minimum and residence
requirements.summary: A bachelor degree requires at least 120 credits and a 2.0 GPA both overall and in Miami work; a college or program may impose a higher threshold. At least half of major credits must be earned at Miami. Correspondence/extension credit combined is limited to 30 and cannot be part of the last 45; examinations and other nonregistration credit cannot satisfy the final residence requirement.

requirements.title: Final 45-credit university residency
requirements.summary: The final 45 degree credits must be completed through Miami. Transfer credit does not satisfy this requirement; an extenuating-circumstances appeal follows the school or college procedure. Miami-sponsored study abroad is Miami coursework rather than transfer work.

requirements.title: Applicable bulletin and declarations
requirements.summary: Degree requirements follow the bulletin applicable at admission to the degree program. After interrupted enrollment, readmitted students normally follow their original requirements but may request a newer bulletin through their school. Current administrative procedures still apply. The individual Degree Progress Report and approved declarations determine the student-specific record; this inventory does not access that private record.

requirements.title: Areas of Knowledge and cognate choice rules
requirements.summary: Complete Arts and Humanities, People and Society, and STEM Areas of Knowledge, normally through a nine-credit thematic or individualized cognate or an assigned major/minor. A course can satisfy only one area cognate, and the overall set must contain at least three subject codes. Thematic cognates must have different responsible academic units; no more than two areas can use units in one school, except Arts and Sciences. A major/minor assigned multiple areas satisfies only one. Substitutions and unspecified transfer work require the responsible unit approval; individualized cognates require the explicit course area attribute without exceptions.

requirements.title: Written communication and primary-major advanced writing
requirements.summary: Complete WRS 105 and WRS 106, WRS 107 or ENG 106, or approved equivalents, before junior classification. Accepted AP/IB may satisfy the requirement; qualifying SAT/ACT can exempt WRS 105 without credit. Approved incoming college writing credit may allow WRS 208 in place of one course. College and major advanced-writing rules remain additional.

requirements.title: Advanced writing for multiple majors or degrees
requirements.summary: Advanced writing and communication follows the school, college and major requirements. With multiple majors, the primary major governs; with two degrees, both degree requirements apply.

requirements.title: Business coursework residence and study abroad
requirements.summary: After admission to Miami, all business coursework for business and non-business students must be taken in residence unless a written exception is approved. Miami-sponsored study abroad counts in residence, but at most one course with a clear international/global business focus may count toward a business major/minor/cognate with approved equivalence. Required core and other discipline-required courses must be on campus; non-Miami study abroad receives no business equivalence.

requirements.title: Business repeat and threshold restrictions
requirements.summary: Business coursework permits at most two completions, including equivalent course pairs, and a repeated course must receive a letter grade. Threshold courses can be repeated to establish the required grade. C-minus that is insufficient for a major/minor must use the general repeat rule, not the undergraduate replacement rule. Replacement repeats must be in residence; summer sessions do not consume the two-regular-semester window.

requirements.title: Business degree GPA, residence and exclusions
requirements.summary: BBA and BSBA require at least 120 credits, minimum 2.5 in both the combined UM-plus-transfer and Miami-only GPA, and 2.5 in each business major/minor. The last 45 credits must be consecutive and exclusive degree-seeking residence at Miami Business; examination credit does not count. WRS 103, TAL 191, MTH 099 and UMI 105–410 do not count toward the degree. Applied music, including band, is capped at eight elective credits; science electives preparing for medical school must be graded.

requirements.title: Business external and internal transfer admission
requirements.summary: External transfer requires good prior standing, cumulative transfer GPA of at least 3.0 and B or better in MTH 161, MTH 151, both MTH 140/141, or Miami-equivalent MTH 171. Internal transfer requires at least 3.0 Miami GPA and the same calculus threshold before the final four degree semesters; calculus may be repeated once to reach B. Submit the Navigate internal-transfer request for end-of-semester review and formal academic change. External transfer students must complete at least half the business core and half each major/minor at Miami.

requirements.title: Business academic progression and readmission
requirements.summary: The school reviews semester or cumulative GPA below 2.0 and inadequate progress. Progress includes passing repeated core/major/minor courses, completing the required calculus before the fifth semester, maintaining a feasible path to the 2.5 graduation/major GPA and finishing within ten regular semesters. More than one semester below 2.0 combined GPA may lead to discontinued enrollment review; appeals are due within 30 days. Readmission after poor standing requires changed circumstances; without C in MAS 110 or MTH 161 business readmission is unavailable.

requirements.title: Business cognate and declaration constraints
requirements.summary: The AI business major supplies STEM. Complete an Arts and Humanities cognate outside Business and meet People and Society through an appropriate cognate or qualifying major/minor. Declare cognates, majors and minors with the Cane Navigator before junior year. At least one business major is required; additional majors/minors are optional and may increase total credits.

requirements.title: Business overlap exceptions and program-specific restrictions
requirements.summary: General business policy allows overlap only when a numbered course is explicitly required by both specializations, potentially with replacement coursework; choice electives cannot double count. An outside-school additional major cannot reuse business-major/minor courses. The AI program’s stricter local no-double-counting rule remains controlling in this record; no general exception is silently applied to it.

requirements.title: Student-selected cognates and declaration
requirements.summary: A cognate has at least three courses and nine credits. Students select their cognates and declare them through their home college by the end of sophomore year. A major/minor does not prescribe a specific cognate outside its own Area of Knowledge; thematic substitutions require responsible-unit approval.

requirements.title: Individualized cognate restrictions
requirements.summary: Each individualized cognate needs at least three courses and nine credits with the same Area of Knowledge attribute in CaneLink. Its courses cannot also fulfill any other degree requirement, including quantitative proficiency. CR grades are excluded except eligible test credit with a specific Miami equivalency. This stricter statement is specific to individualized cognates, not a prohibition on all thematic cognate/major relationships.

outcomes.text: Apply AI to business problems and deploy systems on cloud platforms.
Design intelligent agents for business automation.
Evaluate legal, ethical and societal implications of business AI.
Use AI in marketing, finance and operations and collaborate across disciplines.
